why: B (abstract M, any Levi-Civita cov, n ≥ 1, blind geodesic γ on [0,1]): (a) parallel fields orthonormal at one t₀ ∈ [0,1] are orthonormal on [0,1]; (b) there are parallel P₁..Pₙ along γ on [0,1], orthonormal everywhere, with dγ/dt = L·Pₙ (L = arc length, L = 0 allowed). A (universes 0): (1) a smooth clamp ℝ → [−a, 1+a] equal to id on [0,1]; (2) a geodesic γ ∈ Ω(N;p,q) agrees on [0,1] with a smooth c : ℝ → N, γ' = Vf on (0,1), ‖Vf‖ ≡ L, L⁻¹Vf parallel along c; (3) for L > 0, parallel UNIT fields P_i (i ∈ u) along c and s ⊆ u with |s| + 1 = n and the Ricci-sum bound Σ_{i∈s}⟨R(Vf,P_i)Vf,P_i⟩ ≥ L²|s|/r² — the statement of (3) records neither orthogonality of the frame nor Pₙ = Vf/L. A ⇒ B fails genuinely: abstract setting (no existence of parallel transport for an abstract Mathlib connection); B's clause (a) is proved outright from IsCompat (B_clause_a). B ⇒ A fails genuinely: B gives frames on [0,1] only, not A's extension of γ to a smooth curve on ℝ with fields parallel on all of ℝ (A(2), A(3)); A(1) is real analysis. So B has Milnor's orthonormality and V = L·Pₙ, which A's statement lacks; A has the ℝ-extension and the Ricci-sum bound.
